hypothesis: Same build as exp-rayon-io, re-measured on the boxes as they are now. The boxes were idle-stopped and restarted (likely new physical hosts) between exp-rayon-io and the CPU-feature runs, whose c8g gains (~2.5%) did not stack. If this re-measure also lands near 6.55s on c8g, those gains were host change.
llm_commentary: m8azn.3xlarge (AMD EPYC 9R05, Zen 5 at 5.0 GHz, 12 vCPUs, 48 GiB): stock main 5.76s [5.70/5.75/5.84] → champion 4.52s [4.54/4.50/4.51] on the same boot, -21.5%. With 3x the cores of m8azn.xlarge (5.51s), the client and node no longer fight for CPU, which accounts for a 1s drop at the same clock. It is the fastest box measured (4.52s vs m9g's 4.59s and c8a's 4.76s), but its margin over m9g is 1.5%, inside Graviton5's ~±3% between-run drift and measured on a different boot, so treat the two as tied. At $0.00156 per run it costs ~3x m9g ($0.00050) for that tie: m9g remains the best performance-per-dollar box, and m8azn.3xlarge only makes sense if the extra cores serve more concurrent load than this benchmark generates.
